title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
statement_short: Given the root of a binary tree, return its maximum depth. The maximum depth is the number of nodes along the longest path from the root node down to the farthest leaf node.
constraints: 0 <= number of nodes in tree <= 10^4, -100 <= Node.val <= 100
hint: Tree node count up to 10^4 allows a recursive bottom-up depth calculation in O(n) time.
keywords: longest path from the root node
why_not: Right: Tree DFS recursively computes max(depth(left), depth(right)) + 1 in O(n) time and O(h) call stack space. Not Tree BFS: Level-order traversal using a queue also finds tree depth in O(n) time, but requires O(w) queue space for tree width. Not 1D DP: Dynamic programming table caching is unnecessary for tree post-order depth aggregation. Not Union-Find: Disjoint sets track connected component graphs rather than hierarchical tree depth.
